Meta.title: LocDev — Your local environment, without limits
Meta.description: An open-source local development environment powered by Rust. .test domains, HTTPS, runtimes, and complete workflow control.

Hero.body: Your projects, your domains, your environment. One Rust daemon connecting CLI, desktop, DNS, and HTTPS — no mandatory cloud, no subscriptions, no friction.
Hero.caption: YOUR WORKSPACE. YOUR RULES.

FAQ.title: No tricks. No fine print.

a1.p1: Yes. LocDev is free and open source, distributed under the Apache-2.0 license. You do not need a subscription to use the essential local development features.
a1.p2: You may use LocDev for personal, academic, professional, and commercial projects, including work for clients. The license allows you to study, modify, and redistribute the source code, provided you comply with its terms, including applicable license notices.
a1.p3: The goal is to give you the freedom to work across stacks in one tool without putting essential functionality behind a subscription. Some features are still being developed, and availability depends on your installed version. You can follow the code, suggest improvements, and contribute on GitHub.

a2.p1: No. LocDev’s core workflow does not require Docker, Podman, or a virtual machine. Development servers run as native processes on your computer, managed by a local daemon.
a2.p2: The CLI and desktop app communicate with that same daemon. It registers projects, starts and stops processes, routes requests through the proxy, and provides features such as local domains and HTTPS. You can work with Laravel, Next.js, and other applications without setting up containers for every site.
a2.p3: This does not mean every project runs without additional dependencies: PHP, Node.js, databases, and other services may be required by your stack. LocDev runs everything as native processes, without containers.

FAQ.q3: Can I use Linux, Windows, and macOS?

a3.p1: LocDev is designed for Linux, Windows, and macOS. Its shared Rust foundation powers the daemon, CLI, and core functionality, while the desktop app uses Tauri.
a3.p2: Installation and behavior can vary by operating system. Local DNS configuration, HTTPS certificate trust, automatic startup services, and required dependencies use each platform’s own mechanisms.
a3.p3: Platform support is evolving, and installer validation or specific workflows may still be pending. Before installing, check the requirements, available artifacts, and release notes to verify compatibility with your machine.

a4.p1: Not yet for critical environments. LocDev remains in prerelease, with packaging, compatibility, and binary signing still undergoing validation.
a4.p2: Available builds can be useful for trying the app, testing features, and reporting issues. However, an installer or a feature in the source code does not guarantee that it has been validated on every platform or in every usage scenario.
a4.p3: To try it safely, review your platform requirements and the release notes, and keep backups of important configuration. The download page links to available releases; the changelog shows what changed in each version.

Donate.label: Support LocDev
Donate.title: Less friction for developers. More room to keep building.
Donate.body: Keeping LocDev in development takes time: fixing bugs, testing operating systems, tracking runtimes, and improving each interaction. Voluntary support helps sustain this work.
Donate.fundBody: Voluntary contributions go to bnacci through GitHub Sponsors or Buy Me a Coffee.
Donate.noPayment: Payments are handled by GitHub and Buy Me a Coffee. This site doesn't process any payment.
Donate.prioritiesTitle: Maintain what works. Build what comes next.
Donate.prioritiesBody: These priorities come from the work described in the LocDev README, build tools, and changelog. Support could help dedicate more time and resources to them.
Donate.maintenanceBody: Fix issues and keep up with dependencies across the daemon, CLI, HTTP/HTTPS proxy, .test DNS, and local certificates. The foundation that keeps your projects running needs ongoing care.
Donate.experienceBody: Refine desktop workflows, the command palette, logs, and Doctor. Improve messages, accessibility, and documentation to reduce the time between opening a project and writing code.
Donate.runtimesBody: Develop per-project Node.js and PHP versions and maintain the PHP build pipeline, signed manifests, and download verification. These parts need to keep pace with tool updates.
Donate.releasesBody: Expand real-world testing on Linux, macOS, and Windows, validate installers, and work toward signed binaries. Packaging and compatibility are part of the path to a stable release.
Donate.principlesTitle: Support the work, without buying a promise.
Donate.voluntary: LocDev remains an open-source application under Apache-2.0. Support is voluntary and will not be a requirement for using essential local development features.
Donate.plans: Advanced diagnostics and workspaces don't exist in the app yet. A contribution does not buy priority, guarantee a feature, or set a delivery date.
Donate.otherTitle: Contributions do not have to be financial.
Donate.testBody: Try the available builds and describe your system, what happened, and how to reproduce it. This helps turn real-world failures into fixes.
Donate.docsBody: Use the guides, flag confusing steps, and help improve explanations and translations. Clear documentation improves the development experience too.
Donate.codeBody: Fixes, reviews, and interface improvements help move the project forward. Access and contributions follow the repository’s availability and guidelines.
Donate.sourceNote: Priorities are based on the LocDev repository README, changelog, and build documentation. Items not delivered yet remain subject to implementation and validation.

Onboarding.title: From download to your first project.
Onboarding.body: Choose your environment and follow the steps to install LocDev and start a project. Every command is available to copy.
Onboarding.choiceNote: Choose the architecture of the machine running the app. Availability depends on the files published in the selected channel.
Onboarding.desktopSteps: Download the matching installer, check its SHA-256, and open the file. The app includes the CLI and daemon as sidecars. To use the next step’s commands, put the CLI on PATH or install the CLI archive separately.
Onboarding.cliSteps: Download the CLI archive, extract locdev and locdevd into the same directory, and add it to PATH. Check the SHA-256 before use.
Onboarding.noPackage: No matching public package is currently available. Check the repository or build from source if you have access.
Onboarding.prerequisites: You need Git, stable Rust, and—for the desktop—Node.js 20+, pnpm, and the Tauri prerequisites for your system.
Onboarding.sourceDesktop: Installers are generated in target/release/bundle. Open the installer for your platform. To use the next step’s commands, put the CLI on PATH or install the CLI archive separately.
Onboarding.sourceCli: Binaries are in target/release (.exe on Windows). Keep locdev and locdevd together and add the directory to PATH.
Onboarding.pathNote: After installation and PATH setup, enter an existing project directory with its dependencies installed. Names below are examples.
Onboarding.missingCommand: Replace <HTTP_SERVER_COMMAND> with the project HTTP command and configure the port assigned by LocDev.
Onboarding.finishNote: The daemon provides PORT and HOST. Generic servers must use these values or the configured port. .localhost needs no DNS setup; .test and HTTPS require the preparation in the docs.

Services.planned: Databases, caches, queues and workers that are marked already run in LocDev; the rest are proposals.
Services.title: Everything that runs alongside your project.
Services.body: Data, queues, workers, scheduled tasks and realtime for each stack. The marked ones already work in LocDev (managed instances, auxiliary processes, Mailbox, Database Manager); the others are proposals, not implemented yet.
Services.scope: Optional ecosystem suggestions. Require the appropriate libraries and project configuration. For UI stacks, databases and queues belong to an associated backend, not the browser.
Services.example: Reference command, assuming installed dependencies. Replace {module} with the actual application module.
Services.embeddedNote: Runs inside the application process or driver. No separate daemon is required; configuration is project-specific.
Services.customNote: The startup command depends on your installation and project.
Services.note: Ports are examples and must be adjusted to avoid conflicts. Alternative workers must not consume the same queue without an explicit choice. SQLite is a local file, not a server. This website does not install or run services.

Services.logoNote: Available logos from SVGL. Services without their own brand use an identified ecosystem logo or a category icon.

supportNote.instances: LocDev creates instances with their own data, port and log, on 127.0.0.1 only, using a system install or a version downloaded with a verified SHA-256.
supportNote.process: When the project has the library, the adapter offers the process; nothing runs before your choice (manual, with the site or never).
supportNote.devServer: LocDev detects the auxiliary server and asks before running it next to the main server.
supportNote.mailbox: LocDev has its own capture SMTP (Mailbox), wired through the site processes' environment; there's no need to install Mailpit.
supportNote.browser: A project file: there is no server. LocDev's Database Manager opens, queries and edits it.
supportNote.proposed: There's no LocDev integration yet; the future integration must review paths, ports, credentials and storage before starting.

About.title: Less setup. More room to build.
About.body: LocDev organizes local development: projects, processes, domains and HTTPS. It brings terminal workflows closer to the desktop, with visible choices and control in your hands.
About.localBody: The daemon and CLI work with local projects. This website presents the app and documentation; it does not execute commands on your machine.
About.controlBody: Commands, permissions and sensitive changes should be understandable. Integrations that have not shipped remain clearly marked as planned.
About.openTitle: A project that can grow with you
About.openBody: Apache-2.0 allows you to use, modify and distribute the code under its conditions. The repository and changelog provide context for contributing.
About.maintainerBody: triooo maintains LocDev and this website. The goal is to improve the development experience and sustain the evolution of the app over time.
About.participateBody: Reproducible reports, documentation, translations and code contributions help the project. Financial support is available through GitHub Sponsors and Buy Me a Coffee.

Privacy.title: Understand what happens to your data.
Privacy.body: This information describes the LocDev website, maintained by triooo. It distinguishes browser processing, external connections and hosting infrastructure.
Privacy.pending: Operational information awaits confirmation. This page should not yet be treated as a completed notice.
Privacy.browserBody: The theme is stored in localStorage under theme. Language navigation may set the functional NEXT_LOCALE cookie. You can remove these in browser settings, which resets your preferences. Google Analytics, through Google Tag Manager, loads only if you turn it on in the cookie panel; the site integrates no advertising. Your cookie notice choice is saved in this browser or only in the current tab, depending on your preference, and can be reviewed using the cookie button.
Privacy.generatorBody: The name, path, command and port entered in Configure are processed in your browser. The generator code does not send these fields to the server. Copying commands and downloading a TOML example are explicit actions; the website does not run your project or change your files.
Privacy.externalBody: The server queries the GitHub API for public releases. When you open GitHub, triooo or external documentation, those sites apply their own practices. Website fonts, logos and screenshots are served by this project. The site has no checkout: financial support happens on GitHub Sponsors or Buy Me a Coffee, under their own policies.
Privacy.hostingBody: The intended hosting platform is Vercel. Infrastructure may process request information and technical records to operate, protect and diagnose the service. This is separate from local generator processing; we do not promise that the platform keeps no logs.
Privacy.retentionDefault: Log availability and retention vary with the Vercel plan and settings. We do not state a universal retention period; contact us to clarify the applicable configuration.
Privacy.appTitle: The application is a separate context
Privacy.appBody: The desktop, CLI and daemon work with your local environment and have their own access boundaries. This page does not replace application security documentation or present future integrations as already available.
Privacy.contactBody: Contact triooo with questions about data processing on this website or your information. Share only what is necessary for us to understand your request.
Privacy.contactPending: The privacy contact will be published after confirmation.
Privacy.changes: This information should be reviewed whenever website hosting, integrations or data flows change.

SecurityReporting.prepareBody: Gather the details that help maintainers understand and reproduce the problem.
SecurityReporting.title: A private channel for security reports.
SecurityReporting.body: If you identify a possible vulnerability in LocDev or this website, share details with triooo by email before disclosing them publicly.
SecurityReporting.privateBody: Use {contact}. Do not open a public issue containing exploitation details, and do not include passwords, tokens, .env files or third-party data.
SecurityReporting.step1: Affected version, operating system and component: website, desktop, CLI or daemon.
SecurityReporting.step2: Minimal reproduction steps and a safe demonstration in an environment you control.
SecurityReporting.step3: Observed impact and evidence with sensitive data removed.
SecurityReporting.process: triooo reviews the report and may request additional information. Coordinate disclosure with the maintainers to allow investigation and a possible fix before public exposure.
SecurityReporting.limits: No response deadline, financial reward or fix is guaranteed. This channel does not authorize testing third-party systems, disrupting services or accessing others’ data.

FaqPage.title: Frequently asked questions
FaqPage.body: Questions before getting started or while using LocDev? Find answers and the next guide to read.
FaqPage.servicesQuestion: Are the catalog services already implemented?

servicesAnswer.p1: Some of them. LocDev already runs PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis and Valkey instances, has its own Mailbox to capture email, and offers queues, schedulers, Horizon, Reverb, Sidekiq and Celery as site auxiliary processes. The other catalog entries are still proposals, and the services page marks each one.
servicesAnswer.p2: Some installs depend on the system: MySQL and Redis have no verifiable official binaries, so LocDev uses the system ones (or MariaDB and Valkey, which it downloads with a verified SHA-256). The managed download hasn't been validated end to end yet.
servicesAnswer.p3: Before relying on an integration, check its state on the services page, in the documentation and in the changelog for the version you use.

offlineAnswer.p1: Yes, for local tasks that have already been set up. The daemon, proxy, local domain resolution, HTTPS, and project processes run on your own machine without requiring a persistent internet connection.
offlineAnswer.p2: You may still need internet access to download the app, install runtimes or dependencies, update packages, clone repositories, or use external APIs and services. An individual project may also depend on externally hosted databases, authentication, or other resources.
offlineAnswer.p3: In short, LocDev does not require an online account to control your local sites, but each application’s offline capabilities depend on the services and integrations it uses.

FaqPage.updatesQuestion: How do I update or remove LocDev?

updatesAnswer.p1: Read the update documentation and release notes before replacing binaries. Check requirements and configuration changes, especially while the project is in prerelease.
updatesAnswer.p2: Before updating, back up important configuration and data, and stop processes when the procedure requires it. When uninstalling, remove local DNS integration and certificate authority trust using LocDev commands while the CLI is still available.
updatesAnswer.p3: Removing a registered site does not delete its project files. Still, consult the dedicated uninstall guide to understand which files, startup services, and certificates need to be removed on your operating system.

FaqPage.helpQuestion: What if my project does not start?

helpAnswer.p1: First, check whether the daemon is running. Use `locdev status` and `locdev doctor` to look for configuration, DNS, HTTPS, and software conflicts.
helpAnswer.p2: Then check the startup command, PHP or Node.js versions, installed dependencies, ports, and process output with `locdev logs <site>`. Your project may also need its own settings, such as Vite host permissions.
helpAnswer.p3: If the issue persists, open a GitHub issue with your operating system, LocDev version, steps to reproduce, and relevant logs. Remove passwords, tokens, and personal information before sharing anything. Report security vulnerabilities through the private security channel.

FaqPage.supportBody: Use the support center to choose diagnostics, a bug report or a private security report.

page.title: One environment. Every stack.
page.body: From Laravel to Next.js. From PHP to Node.js. Compare local development environments, feature by feature.
page.fairBody: Our goal is not to claim that one tool replaces all others. Every environment has its specialties, limitations, and execution models.

page.evolutionBody: LocDev is evolving to bring runtimes, services, automation, and developer tools together in an integrated cross-platform interface.

windows.locdev: Native, no WSL or Docker: validated on Windows 11 with static and Laravel sites through the proxy, .test DNS (NRPT), Tinker, worktrees, metrics and the Laravel installer.

opensource.locdev: Apache-2.0, no paid plans or locked features.

wordpress.sail: Requires adaptation; Sail focuses on Laravel.

next.locdev: Detects Next.js and suggests a launch command.
next.herd: Supports Node.js; project-specific integration may require configuration.
next.laragon: Supports Node.js; the Next.js workflow depends on the project.
next.ddev: A generic server can be used; configuration is required.

react.locdev: Native Vite integration: port, host, allowed hosts and HMR through the proxy.

python.locdev: Django, Flask and FastAPI with a dev command and the project's venv; Python versions aren't managed.

static.locdev: Detects index.html and serves it with its own static server (clean URLs, 404.html), no Python or Node needed.

cli.locdev: Every app feature from the terminal too, plus a full-screen TUI (`locdev`).

desktop.lerd: Provides web and TUI interfaces and desktop integration.
desktop.compose: Docker Desktop provides a graphical interface.

runtime.locdev: Detection, per-site pins and installs of official builds (StaticPHP, windows.php.net) only with the publisher's SHA-256; lists each version's extensions.

worktrees.locdev: Each branch in a folder next to the repository, optionally as its own .test site with the .env files copied; removal with a preview and backup.

env.compose: Supports env_file and environment variables; not equivalent to a global secrets manager.

creator.locdev: Laravel (with laravel new's own questions: starter kit, authentication, Livewire, teams), Symfony, Bedrock, Next.js, Vite, Nuxt, Astro, SvelteKit, NestJS, Django, Rails and ASP.NET Core through each one's official installer.

metrics.locdev: Through the proxy: status classes, p50/p95/p99, requests per minute, busiest paths and the latest requests.

tinker.locdev: An editor that runs code (php artisan tinker --execute) and an interactive console, with the site's PHP and environment.

installers.locdev: Each tool's official command (Laravel, Symfony, Bun, uv, WP-CLI, Rust, .NET…) in an app terminal, after it's shown.

mysql.locdev: MariaDB downloaded with a verified SHA-256; MySQL 8.0, 8.4 or the latest installed from the app via Homebrew, apt or winget.

redis.locdev: Valkey downloaded with a verified SHA-256; Redis (several versions) installed from the app via Homebrew or apt.

mail.locdev: Built-in Mailbox: capture-only SMTP on loopback.

why.title: An integrated workflow from local project to deployment
why.body: The advantage is the combination: native execution, multiple stacks and development tools in one application. The matrix identifies equivalent features and competitor integrations that have not been verified.
why.nativeBody: PHP, Node.js and Python projects with local domains, HTTPS and a proxy. Skip building a Docker environment when your projects can run natively.
why.gitBody: Review diffs, commit changes and manage branches. Connect GitHub and prepare workflows with templates, validation and change previews.
why.emailBody: Use Mailbox to receive local messages and Email Studio to discover, edit and preview templates with change history.
why.debugBody: Collect errors and dumps in the Debug Center with secret redaction. Share through tunnels and connect projects to Vercel or Netlify.
why.limitsBody: Git and external providers require their own tools or credentials. Tunnels and deployments depend on those providers and their plans. Python versions aren't managed, and Redis has no official Windows build (use WSL or Memurai there). The Debug Center and the metrics see what goes through the proxy but don't replace a full profiler.
why.evidence: Features verified in source code; availability in your installed version may vary.

AboutApp.subtitle: Versions, license and command line
AboutApp.cliBody: The locdev CLI talks to the same daemon; you can also control your projects from the terminal. Run locdev on its own to open the terminal interface.
AboutApp.cliInstall: In the app, About shows the CLI version and path and lets you add locdev to your terminal for your user, without administrator rights.
AboutApp.description: LocDev brings your projects and development servers together in one place. Start and stop projects, follow their logs, and access each site through a .test domain with local HTTPS, from the app or CLI. Open source for Linux, macOS and Windows.
AboutApp.creditsBody: LocDev is open source under the Apache License 2.0. It's built on open-source software: Tauri, React, Rust's tokio, hyper and rustls, and hundreds more, each under its own license.
AboutApp.packagesBody: The packages inside LocDev's app, daemon and CLI, with the licenses their authors declare. Each keeps its own copyright and license.
AboutApp.installationBody: The running daemon version, build commit and date, system and configuration folder for your installation are available in About in the app.
AboutApp.releaseNote: Published version details; the credits below match the inventory included in the app source code.

InstallationGuide.heroBody: Install LocDev with the app, from the terminal or from source. Choose your system and follow its commands.
InstallationGuide.environmentBody: Choose the system of the machine where you will install LocDev.
InstallationGuide.unavailable: Downloads could not be checked. Try the download page or build from Git.
InstallationGuide.noRelease: No published release in this channel. Building from Git is still available.
InstallationGuide.methodBody: The full app, standalone CLI or a local build: three ways to get started.
InstallationGuide.app_linux: Download the .deb for Debian/Ubuntu, the .rpm for Fedora, or the AppImage to run without installation.
InstallationGuide.app_macos: Open the .dmg and drag LocDev to Applications.
InstallationGuide.app_windows: Run the .exe or .msi installer and follow the on-screen instructions.
InstallationGuide.included: The app includes the daemon and CLI. In Settings → About, you can add locdev to your terminal.
InstallationGuide.downloadThenRun: After downloading, open a terminal in the file’s folder and run:
InstallationGuide.terminalBody: The official script installs locdev and locdevd without a GUI or administrator rights and verifies the archive against SHA256SUMS. It detects the machine architecture automatically.
InstallationGuide.windowsArm: The Windows CLI installer provides x64 only. For ARM64, check available downloads or build natively from Git.
InstallationGuide.windowsPath: Installs in %LOCALAPPDATA%\LocDev\cli and adds it to your user Path. Open a new terminal after installing.
InstallationGuide.unixPath: Installs in ~/.local/bin. The export command below updates this session’s PATH; add the folder to your shell profile to persist it.
InstallationGuide.previewMissing: No preview release is published. Select stable or build from Git.
InstallationGuide.requiresRelease: This command requires a published release with the script, the platform CLI and SHA256SUMS.
InstallationGuide.verify: After installing, check the version and environment:
InstallationGuide.sourceBody: Clone the repository and build the app or CLI on your machine.
InstallationGuide.desktopPrereqs: Prerequisites: Git, stable Rust, Node.js 20+, pnpm and your platform’s Tauri dependencies.
InstallationGuide.cliPrereqs: Prerequisites: Git, stable Rust and the system build tools.
InstallationGuide.desktopOutput: Installers are in target/release/bundle or target/<target>/release/bundle. The build includes the CLI and daemon automatically.
InstallationGuide.cliOutput: The locdev and locdevd binaries are in target/release. Keep them together and add the folder to PATH to run them from any directory.
InstallationGuide.nativeBuild: Build on the target operating system and architecture. These commands use the machine’s native tools; they do not cross-compile.
